clue.text: Hit a couple of equines before one race

indicators.note: before puts the equines ahead of the pieces that follow
a couple means two, so the word for one equine is written twice

parts.note: an ass is an equine, a donkey
one is the Roman numeral I
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A racing tip: back a pair of donkeys ahead of a single race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' is the definition in its gangland sense of a contract killing. 'a couple of' doubles ASS; 'before' puts ASSASS ahead of I and NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is criminal slang for a planned killing of a target.

clue.text: Desire book in excellent cover cut — close to the bone

definitions.text: cover cut — close to the bone

indicators.note: in puts the desire and the book inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means excellent, here spelt out as A ONE
an itch is a desire or craving

explanation.surface: A craving for a book inside a fine binding, with a butcher's cut thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is written as A ONE, and ITCH plus B goes inside it. The aitchbone is the rump bone of cattle and the cut of beef lying over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The butcher's joint of beef from over the rump bone sits right against that bone.

clue.text: Drawn into offence, prepared to testify

indicators.note: into puts the word for drawn inside the word for offence

parts.note: a sin is an offence
drawn, as in tired-looking, means worn

explanation.surface: Someone dragged into a crime is now ready to give evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' in the sense of haggard gives WORN, which goes into SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness takes an oath before giving evidence, so being under oath means ready for the box.

clue.text: Appropriate strike

explanation.surface: Taking a swing at someone is the fitting response.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to steal, slang 'swipe'; a swipe is also a sweeping blow.

clue.text: It completely demolished evaluation with mirth

indicators.note: something completely demolished is knocked down to be rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's assessment was torn apart amid laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun but is the definition: 'It' is short for the drink in 'gin and It'. 'completely demolished' rearranges EVALUATION and MIRTH.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British bar 'gin and It' means gin mixed with sweet red vermouth from Italy, so It names that drink.

clue.text: Nearly last in succession, taking extremely stern position

indicators.note: last says the word for nearly goes at the end

parts.note: coming in succession means coming after
most can mean almost or nearly, as in 'most everyone'

explanation.surface: Close to the end of the line of succession, someone takes a tough stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' gives MOST (almost), placed last, after AFTER. 'last in succession' reads as the definition but supplies two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft means toward the stern, so the most aft part of a ship is at its very back.

clue.text: Second of April, currently?

explanation.surface: A question about the second day of April this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' (instant) in old business letters means of the current month, so 'the 2nd inst.' written in April means the second of April.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a moment; and 'instant' in letters marks a date in this present month.

clue.text: Proverbially hard things to find at one's fingertips

definitions.text: things to find at one's fingertips

explanation.surface: Hard facts proverbially kept close to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tough is 'hard as nails'; and keratin plates grow at the ends of fingers.

clue.text: Emperor's reflective treatment of religious work

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a religious work

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the second copy is read backwards

parts.note: the Old Testament again, abbreviated OT

explanation.surface: An emperor's thoughtful study of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective treatment of' adds a mirror image of OT, giving TO, so the whole reads the same both ways. Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto I and later rulers of that name held the title Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: E.g. unable to draw cart — it is in to be fixed

indicators.note: something to be fixed must be put right, so the letters need rearranging

explanation.surface: A horse can't pull the cart because it's in for repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' tempts as pulling a cart, but the definition means unable to draw pictures. 'to be fixed' rearranges CART IT IS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no flair for art or sketching is lacking artistic skill.

clue.text: Grand light music finally produced by composer? That's right

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of music

parts.note: Handel was a German-born British composer
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A grand piece of light music written by a composer: that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light music' looks like a genre, but 'light' belongs to the definition. 'finally' gives C, the end of 'music'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand branched lamp hung from a ceiling is an ornate light fitting.

clue.text: Showing up in Royal Society as well

indicators.note: showing up in means appearing inside the run of letters Royal Society

explanation.surface: Turning up at the Royal Society too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean in addition or too.

clue.text: Decline — or decline after switching parts

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase change places, so the front part moves to the end

parts.note: to decline an offer is to turn it down

explanation.surface: A fall, or refusing something once the order changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Decline' is a noun (a fall); the second is a verb, TURN DOWN, whose halves swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop in prices or business activity is called a slump.

clue.text: Discover line unknown to mathematicians — that's weird

parts.note: to unearth something is to discover it
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A line no mathematician knows about turns out to be strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supernatural or eerie seems not of this world, hence strange.

clue.text: Ban the wife's mother, say? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the opposite is taken, so the word for in is swapped for its contrary, out

parts.note: a wife's mother is a mother-in-law, an example of an in-law

explanation.surface: A husband wants to keep his mother-in-law away, but it's the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' turns IN of INLAW into its opposite, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to prohibit it.

clue.text: Creative female worked in art houses

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman who made things in art studios.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who writes books is a creative female writer.

clue.text: Tenant not so easily ejected, initially

parts.note: less means not so much

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of easily and ejected

explanation.surface: A renter who can't be evicted so easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a lease, renting property from its owner.

clue.text: Another pound added, tucking into hot German loaf

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so the pound goes within the word for hot

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra); 'another' because the word already holds one L

explanation.surface: Gaining an extra pound by tucking into a hot German bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating but puts L into STOLEN (hot as in stolen goods). Stollen is a fruit loaf eaten at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a sweet fruited bread from Germany, eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: The whole thing is about religious education

indicators.note: is about means goes round, so the word for thing surrounds the education

parts.note: an entity is a thing
RE is the school subject religious education

explanation.surface: The whole subject concerns religious education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The whole thing' reads as the definition, but 'thing' gives ENTITY around RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety of something is the whole of it.

clue.text: Runs I later scrambled in the second test?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled, so I LATER is rearranged

explanation.surface: A batsman scrambles runs late in the second Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: a Test is an international match. The definition means a court case tried a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A case heard again in court puts the accused through a second trial.

clue.text: Australian base announced for capital

indicators.note: announced means said aloud, so the sound of the phrase gives the answer

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia and low means base

explanation.surface: An Australian military base is named as the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: OZ (Australia) plus LOW (base) said aloud sounds like the Norwegian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Succeeded, given court power to launch sudden raid

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Someone who succeeded, given legal power, mounts a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Police or birds of prey that dive down suddenly on a target make a rapid attack.

clue.text: Thinking about maiden's undoing

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for undoing goes round the maiden

parts.note: ruination is someone's undoing
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Contemplating how a young woman was ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumination is deep reflection or pondering.

clue.text: The poor have more of them than the rich

definitions.text: The poor have more of them than the rich

parts.words: The poor have more of them than the rich
parts.note: reads like a remark on possessions, but what the poor have more of is wants and requirements

explanation.definitionFit: Poor people lack necessities, so they have more requirements unmet.

clue.text: Construction featuring in play by children or dramatist

definitions.text: Construction featuring in play by children or dramatist

parts.words: Construction featuring in play by children or dramatist
parts.note: two plays: a toy structure used in children's play, and a drama by Ibsen

explanation.definitionFit: A miniature toy home is used by children at play, and Ibsen wrote a famous drama with this title.

clue.text: A single thing, or a couple

explanation.surface: One object, or two people together.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is one article in a list; two people romantically linked are also called one.

clue.text: Instruments available for change

parts.note: the musical instruments are cheap enough to buy with loose coins, 'change' being small money

explanation.definitionFit: Tin whistles once sold for a penny, so they could be bought with small coins.
